xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF ingested from GitHub issue #4426

plan.title: design(scope,verify): setup-created scopes carry no forge origin, so four lifecycle detectors silently no-op at exit 0 and scope:complete reports a vacuous acceptance

narratives.Description: design(scope,verify): setup-created scopes carry no forge origin, so four lifecycle detectors silently no-op at exit 0 and scope:complete reports a vacuous acceptance
narratives.Overview:
**TL;DR:** The reconciliation layer is keyed on a GitHub issue/PR origin. The setup / greenfield allocation path creates scopes with no linked issue and no `plan.references`. Every detector that would notice a drifted scope then degrades to a silent no-op at exit 0 — and `scope:complete` completes the scope anyway, reporting an acceptance walk that verified nothing. This is the same allocation path as #4383 (setup-created scopes born undeclared); the consequence is not just a missing acceptance oracle, it is a lifecycle that no gate can see.

## What happened

Greenfield consumer on Directive 0.115.0 (`@deftai/directive@0.115.0`, `@deftai/directive-core@0.115.0`), 7 setup-created scopes, no GitHub issues created at allocation. Two scopes were then built:

- `core-engine` — merged as PR #1.
- `wasm-bridge` — built, PR #4 open and merge-blocked.

Both briefs remained in `xbrief/active/` with `status: running`. No detector reported anything, and no verb asked.

## Evidence — four silent no-ops, all exit 0

Neither brief contains a `plan.references` array, so `collectGithubRefs` (`orphan-active/refs.js:71-93`) returns zero issues and zero PRs, and `evaluate.js:414` skips the brief.

**1. Orphan sweep** — reports clean while a merged-PR scope sits active:

```
$ deft verify:orphan-active
verify:orphan-active: no orphaned active/running xBRIEFs (scanned 2 running briefs in active/).
  Basis: no GitHub lookups.
exit=0
```

**2. Closeout attestability** — reuses the same #3240 gate that `scope:complete` enforces, and no-ops:

```
$ deft verify:pr-closeout-attestable --pr 4
verify:pr-closeout-attestable: PR #4 closes no issue; closeout attestability does not apply.
exit=0
```

**3. Completed-tracked sweep** — "nothing to check" while the drift is present:

```
$ deft verify:completed-tracked
verify:completed-tracked: no scoped lifecycle origins found; nothing to check.
exit=0
```

The same verifier, handed the number, finds it immediately:

```
$ deft verify:completed-tracked --issue 1
verify:completed-tracked: 1 closed scoped issue lack a tracked xbrief/completed/ or xbrief/cancelled/ artifact on delivery tip origin/master (project_root=...).
  Remediation: task swarm:finalize-cohort (or open a lifecycle PR that lands the completed/cancelled xBRIEFs).
  Missing:
    - deftai/bs-deepwordle#1 (origin: --issue 1)
exit=1
```

So the detector is functional but unsweepable on this path: it fires only when a caller already knows the number, and nothing supplies one.

**4. The completion path itself** — completes and reports the vacuous walk:

```
$ deft scope:complete xbrief/active/2026-09-11-core-engine.xbrief.json
Completed 2026-09-11-core-engine.xbrief.json: active/ -> completed/ (status: completed)
Acceptance criteria: (none)
verify:ac clause walk (#3323): 0 verified, 5 unverifiable, 0 failed
  [unverifiable] clause 1 @ (no path): A game can be created from a secret word ... — no artifact path bound
  ... (all 5 clauses "no artifact path bound")
verify:ac passed (#3284) [rung=derived]
Literal acceptance-command gate: no stated commands (nothing to run) (#3284/#3267)
work-claim release skipped: no github-issue origin
exit=0
```

Reproduced in a copy of the repo at the same SHA (`61be57e`) with `.git` intact. No delivery-evidence refusal fired; the verb wrote `active/` → `completed/`.

Note the last line: the framework **knows** the origin is missing and degrades silently. `work-claim release skipped: no github-issue origin` is the same root as `orphan-active`'s "no GitHub lookups" and `pr-closeout-attestable`'s "closes no issue".

## Root cause — two things, not one

The drift has exactly two causes, and neither is a blocked write path.

**1. Nothing forces the bookkeeping.** The task ledger and the scope's lifecycle status are updated only when an agent bundles those edits into a commit. Same tooling, opposite outcomes on this project: `core-engine`'s ledger (`history/changes/core-engine/tasks.xbrief.json`) was added in the code commit (`39c5e6d`) all-`pending` and never touched again after PR #1 merged; `wasm-bridge`'s was flipped to `completed` in its own code commit (`396e5a4`). The only variable is recall. Owned by #4385.

**2. Nothing detects the absence on the sweep.** All four detectors above no-op at exit 0 on the issue-less path. The scoped form works — `verify:completed-tracked --issue 1` exits 1 — but nothing supplies the number.

**A hypothesis that was tested and falsified**, recorded so it is not re-derived: the first reading of this situation was that `scope:complete` is structurally blocked by unbound acceptance clauses, so the scope *could not* be closed. It is not blocked. In a copy of the repo at the same SHA (`61be57e`) the verb completes at exit 0 while printing `0 verified, 5 unverifiable` and `work-claim release skipped: no github-issue origin`. The #3240 per-item evidence gate walks `plan.items` **on the brief**, which is empty here (the six items live in the history ledger), so it passes with `Acceptance criteria: (none)`. The close-out path is available and vacuous — it is not gated. Any fix premised on "the verb refuses" would be aimed at the wrong layer.

## Why it is origin-keyed

Scopes are allocated two ways: from a GitHub issue (decompose / triage) and from the setup interview (greenfield). Only the first records forge identity. Every downstream detector is origin-keyed, so on the second path detection is not merely offline — there is no origin to resolve, and each verb converts "nothing to resolve" into "nothing wrong". The asymmetry is visible in a single run: `verify:completed-tracked --issue 1` proves the drift is detectable, and the bare sweep proves nothing asks.

## Acceptance sketch

- [ ] An active/running brief with no resolvable forge origin reports a distinct non-clean outcome (`origin_unresolved`), never a silent skip
- [ ] `verify:orphan-active` distinguishes "0 scanned" from "N clean" in its output and exit code
- [ ] `verify:completed-tracked` bare sweep distinguishes "no origins exist" from "origins exist and none are resolvable"
- [ ] `scope:complete` does not print `verify:ac passed` for a 0-verified walk; an entirely unbound clause set is a refusal, not `Acceptance criteria: (none)`
- [ ] Setup or activation records an origin reference, or the framework states explicitly that issue-less scopes are outside the reconciliation model

Refs #4383, #4380, #4385, #3913, #3910, #3790, #3429, #3476

### Comment by @visionik (2026-09-11T20:30:39Z)

## Second instance, and the walk cannot pass for the right reason either

A second setup-created scope reproduced this on the same consumer, and probing it turned up something sharper than "the clauses are unbound". **`deftai/bs-deepwordle`, `server-api` scope, brief `xbrief/active/2026-09-11-server-api.xbrief.json`.**

All four clauses are implemented and each maps to code with tests that fail if the behaviour is removed:

| clause | artifact |
| --- | --- |
| 1. An endpoint issues a game and returns a game ID. | `internal/server/http.go` `handleIssue`, `TestIssueGameReturnsTheShapeAndNotTheWord` |
| 2. A submission endpoint replays guesses against the stored answer and rejects inconsistent sequences. | `internal/server/replay.go` `Replay`, `replay_test.go` |
| 3. The SQLite schema stores games, guess sequences, per-player aggregates, and leaderboard rows. | `internal/server/store.go`, `store_test.go` |
| 4. Client-submitted results are rejected unless replay validation succeeds. | `internal/server/http.go` `handleSubmit`, `TestAnUnexpectedFailureIsAnInternalError` |

The gate, verbatim:

```
$ deft verify:ac xbrief/active/2026-09-11-server-api.xbrief.json
verify:ac clause walk (#3323): 0 verified, 4 unverifiable, 0 failed
  [unverifiable] clause 1 @ (no path): An endpoint issues a game and returns a game ID. — no artifact path bound
  [unverifiable] clause 2 @ (no path): A submission endpoint replays guesses against the stored answer and rejects inconsistent sequences. — no artifact path bound
  [unverifiable] clause 3 @ (no path): The SQLite schema stores games, guess sequences, per-player aggregates, and leaderboard rows. — no artifact path bound
  [unverifiable] clause 4 @ (no path): Client-submitted results are rejected unless replay validation succeeds. — no artifact path bound
verify:ac passed (#3284) [rung=derived]
Literal acceptance-command gate: no stated commands (nothing to run) (#3284/#3267)
```

Setup Phase 3 wrote all four with `artifact_path: null` and `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope` absent. Same as `core-engine` (`0 verified, 5 unverifiable`), except here I can state with confidence that the clauses *are* met, which makes the `passed` verdict demonstrably wrong rather than merely uninformative.

### Probing it: three degradation levels, and what `failed` actually measures

I probed a copy at the same SHA (real repo verified clean afterwards). Binding a clause is not enough on its own.

**(a) Unbound** — `no artifact path bound`, passes.

**(b) Bound, but the path is not declared in `file_scope`** — still unverifiable, and the reason changes:

```
  [unverifiable] clause 1 @ internal/server/http.go: An endpoint issues a game and returns a game ID.
      — artifact path is not declared on plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope, so nothing was read: internal/server/http.go (#3835)
```

Binding clause 1 to a real file **and** clause 2 to a path that does not exist gives the same `unverifiable` for both — a nonexistent file bound outside `file_scope` does not even register as missing. Still `verify:ac passed`.

**(c) Bound *and* declared in `file_scope`** — now clause 2 fails, because the file is absent:

```
verify:ac clause walk (#3323): 0 verified, 3 unverifiable, 1 failed
  [failed] clause 2 @ internal/server/does-not-exist.go: ... — artifact missing at stated path internal/server/does-not-exist.go
  [unverifiable] clause 1 @ internal/server/http.go: ... — cannot evaluate behavioral claim against shipped artifact internal/server/http.go
verify:ac FAILED (#3284) [rung=derived]
```

That last line is the finding. With everything bound correctly, clause 1 — a **behavioural** clause pointing at the real artifact that implements it — is still `unverifiable`, with the reason *"cannot evaluate behavioral claim against shipped artifact"*.

So across all three levels:

- `verified` requires a stamped, run acceptance command; `plan.acceptance.commands` is empty on this path (`Literal acceptance-command gate: no stated commands (nothing to run)`).
- `failed` is reachable **only** for `artifact missing at stated path` — a *procedural* defect.
- An unmet **behavioural** claim has no representation at all. It is folded into `unverifiable`, which does not fail.

**The walk can fail on a missing file and cannot fail on a requirement that is not met.** For a scope whose clauses are all behavioural — which is what clauses are for — the verdict is decorative in every configuration: unbound it passes, bound it passes, bound-and-correct it passes, and the only thing that makes it stop passing is a typo in a path.

### Sharpening the acceptance sketch

The existing sketch has *"`scope:complete` does not print `verify:ac passed` for a 0-verified walk"*. I'd add:

- [ ] A behavioural clause bound to a real, in-scope artifact must not report `passed` while remaining `unverifiable`. Either the claim is checkable against something (a command, a test name, a symbol) or the brief is refused before completion.
- [ ] `unverifiable` must be distinguishable from `verified` **at the exit code**, not only in the prose. Today `0 verified, N unverifiable` and `N verified, 0 unverifiable` both exit 0 and both print `passed`.
- [ ] `artifact missing at stated path` is the only failing condition; document that the walk is a path-existence check, or extend it so a behavioural clause has a way to fail.

The distinction I'd draw from the two instances: `core-engine` showed the walk reporting a pass it had not earned. `server-api` shows it **cannot** earn one — the success and failure modes for behavioural acceptance are both unreachable from an unbound-or-bound-but-behavioural brief.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-11T21:14:43Z)

Round 1 critic, fresh, refutation charter, N=1. Input ceiling 5640576937 (inclusive); both thread comments at or below it are in envelope. All checks below were run against the dispatch SHA `24867a867124743197cead9b5314a2cf31a4c26b` by reading the TypeScript sources and task descriptors, not the compiled `.js` line numbers the body cites.

**Re-verification scope, stated plainly.** I confirmed all six anchors as *mechanisms* at the pinned SHA. I did **not** re-run the consumer transcripts: `bs-deepwordle` is not in this dest and the run posture is no-ingest. That distinction matters for finding 6.

Anchors confirmed at the pinned SHA: `collectGithubRefs` reads only `plan.references[]` and `plan.metadata["x-tracking"]` (`packages/core/src/orphan-active/refs.ts:98,107,127`); the orphan sweep increments `scanned` at `evaluate.ts:577` and then `continue`s on empty refs at `:583`; `verify:completed-tracked` returns `no scoped lifecycle origins found` at `completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:617`; `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` returns `closes no issue` at `pr-closeout-attestable/evaluate.ts:381`; `Acceptance criteria: (none)` comes from a zero-report `plan.items` walk (`scope/acceptance-evidence.ts:577,581,620`); and setup writes `references` only "when the scope originates from a GitHub issue" (`content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md:769`). The observations are real. Four of the five acceptance criteria drawn from them are not implementable as written.

## 1. `blocks-the-design` — sketch bullet 4 is a `#3826` reversal the lean does not declare, and the same remedy was refused on #4380 one day earlier on this same brief file

**Evidence.** `content/docs/plan-acceptance.md` landed at this SHA (`3dbd7e30b`, `fix(verify-ac): keep clause-walk counts in the pass lead (#4380)`) and states: *"A later lean that wants zero-verified to fail closed MUST reverse `#3826` and name the reader (`standalone` / `check` / `complete`)."* The same MUST is carried in code at `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance-resolver.ts:311`. The #4380 bound remedy (comment 5636518980) reads: *"Keep the #3826 no-oracle excusal on pre-product check... If a later lean wants fail-closed, say it reverses #3826 and name the reader."* The #4240 operator recut locks the adjacent half: *"Do not restore `verified.length > 0` as a set predicate."* The recorded decision `xbrief/decisions/2026-08-28-the-verify-ac-verified-0-requirement-binds-only-when-at-least-on.decision.json` is `confidence: high`, and its `revisitTrigger` fires on exactly this observation — so the trigger is the substantiation the lean needs, and it is not cited.

**Failure mode.** Implemented literally — "an entirely unbound clause set is a refusal" — `scope:complete` refuses every setup-created scope. Binding requires `plan.metadata.swarm.file_scope`, which setup never writes (#4383, open). Adding it post-activation trips `verify_scope_provenance` (#3145), and the remediation `scope:record-approved-scope` refuses an agent shell (#3110). The result is a scope that cannot complete and cannot be repaired in-band: precisely the "unsatisfiable by correct work" state the #3826 decision was made to remove.

**Disposition consequence.** Bullet 4 cannot bind as written. It binds only if restated as an explicit `#3826` reversal scoped to the `complete` reader alone, and sequenced behind #4383. Otherwise drop it.

## 2. `blocks-the-design` — sketch bullet 2's exit-code clause collides with a recorded prohibition, and its output clause is already shipped

**Evidence.** `content/docs/orphan-active-verdict-basis.md` splits the two readers deliberately: scoped `--issue N` fails closed on unknown, the unscoped aggregate fails open, and *"⊗ Do not flatten the two unknown policies into one rule"* — because *"hard-failing every aggregate unknown would break `--skip-gh`, offline runs, and fresh clones."* Meanwhile the output half already exists: `evaluate.ts:626` prints `scanned N running briefs`, and `BasisTally.summary()` (`:208`) prints `no GitHub lookups` when nothing was resolved. The issue body's own transcript shows both lines.

**Failure mode.** Making the bare sweep non-zero on unresolved origins fails `task check`, pre-commit and pre-push in every offline run and every fresh clone. That is the flatten the doc prohibits.

**Disposition consequence.** Drop "and exit code", or scope it to the already-fail-closed `--issue` reader. The output half should be restated as the actual gap: `scanned` counts briefs, nothing counts briefs that resolved zero origins. Adding a `noOrigin` counter to the existing `OrphanActiveBasis` and basis line is an extension of a shipped reporting surface, not a new `origin_unresolved` state.

## 3. `blocks-the-design` — sketch bullet 3 does not cover the reported case, and the `--issue 1` exhibit does not prove what the body says it proves

**Evidence.** When `--issue N` is passed and no brief-derived origin matches, `evaluateCompletedTracked` **synthesizes** one (`completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:596-612`, #3476), with the origin string literally `--issue N`. The body's own output prints `(origin: --issue 1)` — that is the synthetic row. No brief was read to reach it, and nothing in the repository links `core-engine` to issue #1; that linkage came from the operator typing `1`.

**Failure mode.** On the reported path `scanLocalOrigins` yields zero hits, because the briefs carry zero references. So "origins exist and none are resolvable" is false — no origins exist. A fix satisfying bullet 3 literally still reports green on `bs-deepwordle`, and the criterion certifies a change that does not fix the case that motivated it.

**Disposition consequence.** Restate bullet 3 in terms of *briefs scanned versus origins resolved*, not *origins exist versus resolvable*. And drop "the detector is functional but unsweepable" from the substantiation: what `--issue 1` demonstrates is that issue #1 is closed with no tracked terminal artifact, not that the drift is detectable from the brief.

## 4. `blocks-the-design` (injection / swarm lens) — sketch bullet 5's first arm hands an agent a field that steers live forge reads, before the approval that would govern it

The lens fires: the target changes identity recording and lifecycle shared state.

**Evidence.** `collectGithubRefs` resolves `plan.metadata["x-tracking"].parent_issue` and `.decomposition_origin` through `parseTrackingIssue`, which accepts a bare `#N` string, and `addIssueRef` resolves a null repo against `defaultRepo` (`refs.ts:127`, `:52-70`). Setup writes scopes to `xbrief/proposed/` (`SKILL.md:840`) — before any `#3145` approved-scope digest exists (#4383, open). The framework already records the rule for the sibling field: `file_scope` is *"Operator. ⊗ Agent-invented paths."* (`content/docs/plan-acceptance.md`). No equivalent rule guards the origin reference.

**Failure mode.** A setup agent — or issue prose composed verbatim into the brief Overview by `composeOverviewWithComments` — writes a plausible-but-wrong `parent_issue: "#1"`. `verify:orphan-active` then resolves that issue as open and reports clean, permanently, with `Basis: inventory 1` instead of `no GitHub lookups`. Today's defect is a silent skip that the basis line *discloses*; this remedy converts it into a silent false negative that the basis line affirmatively *certifies*. That is strictly worse than the state being fixed.

**Disposition consequence.** Bullet 5 must name the writer, and it cannot be the agent. `task issue:emit` (`tasks/issue.yml:39`) is the existing mechanism that mints a real forge object rather than asserting one; operator-collected is the other. An agent-asserted origin needs the same ⊗ its `file_scope` sibling already carries.

## 5. `sharpens-framing` — issue-less scopes are already a supported, operator-elected mode; the single-writer defect is that setup Phase 3 never offers the choice

**Evidence.** `content/strategies/emit-hints.md` activates *"at the emission step, right after a strategy writes scope vBRIEFs to `xbrief/proposed/`"*, names three tracking patterns — **none** / umbrella / per-vBRIEF — and states *"The user picks one — or takes no action (the default)"* and *"No issue is filed unless the user explicitly invokes `task deft:issue:emit`."* Eleven strategy files under `content/strategies/` reference it. `content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` does not: grep for `emit-hints`, `issue:emit` or `issue-emit` over that file returns nothing, while `:840` writes scope xBRIEFs to `xbrief/proposed/` — the exact emission step emit-hints declares itself active at. `task issue:emit` is live (`tasks/issue.yml:39`, `ENGINE_CMD: issue-emit`), and `content/conventions/references.md` already carries a D11 origin-provenance check over `plan.references`, at warning severity.

**Failure mode.** The operator is never offered the tracking choice, so `none` becomes a default nobody elected — and at sweep time "elected none" and "never asked" are indistinguishable to a detector. Framed as the lean frames it, the remedy surface is four verbs and a new `origin_unresolved` outcome. Framed at the actual writer, it is one skill pointer to a rendered hint plus a verb that already ships.

**Disposition consequence.** The refutation target's causal claim should be restated: origin-keying is not the defect, the unoffered election is. And bullet 5's second arm — *"or the framework states explicitly that issue-less scopes are outside the reconciliation model"* — asks for a statement emit-hints already makes, so it is satisfied on arrival and should be struck rather than built.

## 6. `sharpens-framing` — the transcripts predate the dispatch SHA; the bare `passed` line bullet 4 reacts to is already gone

**Evidence.** Every transcript in the body and in comment 5640274557 is from `@deftai/directive@0.115.0`. `3dbd7e30b` is not an ancestor of `v0.115.0` and is an ancestor of `24867a867`. At the dispatch SHA the lead is composed by `relabelVerifyAcPassLead` as `verify:ac passed (#3284) (0 verified, N unverifiable) [rung=derived]` (`acceptance-resolver.ts:333`).

**Failure mode.** Bullet 4's first clause — *"`scope:complete` does not print `verify:ac passed` for a 0-verified walk"* — reads as a request for a change that landed before dispatch. An arc that binds on it records a remedy for a symptom that no longer reproduces at its own target revision.

**Disposition consequence.** Re-take the `scope:complete` transcript at the dispatch SHA before binding anything in bullet 4. What survives re-taking is the exit code and the completion, not the label.

## 7. `sharpens-framing` — comment 5640274557's two load-bearing mechanism claims are refuted, and its proposed oracle re-opens `#3835`

**Evidence.** In `walkOne` (`packages/core/src/verify-ac/clauses.ts`), `failed` is returned from **seven** conditions, not one: scratch/buffer path (`:972`), path escaped the project root (`:976`), artifact missing (`:990`), not a shipped file (`:994`), unreadable (`:997`, `:1008`), **artifact exists where the clause requires absence** (`:1000`), and **expected tokens missing from the artifact** (`:1013`). `verified` is returned statically from two: tokens present (`:1017`) and an existence claim (`:1020`). Neither involves a stamped acceptance command. So *"`verified` requires a stamped, run acceptance command"* and *"`failed` is reachable only for `artifact missing at stated path`"* are both false, and *"the only thing that makes it stop passing is a typo in a path"* does not hold — `:1000` and `:1013` are semantic failures.

The true and narrower statement is: a clause carrying no quoted literal and no existence/absence phrasing has no static oracle. That is `#4240`'s recorded, deliberate choice — *"a declared path is not an oracle for a behavioral claim with no extractable tokens... unverifiable, not adjudicable"* (`:1024-1034`) — not an unnoticed gap.

**Failure mode (injection half).** The comment's remedy is that a behavioural claim be *"checkable against something (a command, a test name, a symbol)"*. Deriving a test name or a command from clause prose is the `#3835` shape: untrusted input selecting what the gate reads. The recorded decision resolved that by binding every filesystem touch to the declared `file_scope` surface, and its `whyWinner` records that shape-filtering the prose *"was measured to narrow the attack by zero"*. Executing a prose-named test is strictly worse than reading a prose-named file.

**Disposition consequence.** Do not carry the two refuted claims into the record as substantiation. The comment's three added acceptance bullets restate `#4240`'s locked position and the `#3826` reversal from finding 1; they need the same reader-naming before any of them can bind.

## 8. `footnote` — bullet 4 bundles two gates with different readers

`evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` (#3240) walks `plan.items` (`scope/acceptance-evidence.ts:577,581`) and `Acceptance criteria: (none)` is emitted when that walk yields zero reports (`:620`). The `verify:ac` clause walk is a different gate over `plan.acceptance.clauses`. Bullet 4 names both in one criterion. The body's own root-cause section already separates them. Splitting the criterion is bookkeeping; finding 1 carries the disposition.

## 9. `footnote` — the "four silent no-ops" count is three

`verify:pr-closeout-attestable` reaches `closes no issue` from a live read of the PR's structured closing references (`pr-closeout-attestable/evaluate.ts:350,378-388`); it never reads a brief to decide applicability. Its published contract states the boundary verbatim: *"The trigger is the closing reference, not the branch diff... A PR that leaves an unattested brief WITHOUT closing its issue is unaffected"* (`tasks/verify.yml:586`). A brief-keyed `origin_unresolved` outcome cannot reach that decision point, and making "closes no issue" non-clean would refuse every chore, docs and release PR in this repository — `24867a867` closes no issue. This does not change the lean's disposition, which stands on the other three.

## Road not taken

I audited the acceptance sketch bullet-by-bullet against recorded decisions rather than contesting origin-keying as an architecture. The rejected fork was to argue the reconciliation layer should key on brief identity rather than forge identity. I rejected it because Stop 3 is process-only and the arc is refutation-chartered against a recorded target: an architecture counter-proposal is successor-lean work, and a critic that substitutes one would leave the sketch — the thing that actually binds — unexamined.

## Steelman

The strongest position against finding 5: the `none` option in emit-hints was written for strategy-emitted scopes an operator consciously keeps local, and a greenfield interview that produces seven scopes the operator has just committed to building is materially different. Under that reading the detectors really are the defect, because "elected none" and "never asked" are indistinguishable at sweep time regardless of who should have asked — which is close to the lean's own claim that the verbs convert *nothing to resolve* into *nothing wrong*.

What would flip my verdict: a recorded statement that setup Phase 3 deliberately declines the emit-hint, or evidence that this consumer was offered the tracking choice and declined it. I found neither at the pinned SHA — `deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` contains no reference to `emit-hints`, `issue:emit`, or `issue-emit`. If such a record exists, finding 5 drops to a footnote and the lean's causal framing stands as filed. Findings 1 through 4 are unaffected either way.

## Census
